test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 21 March, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.

Dad said that, "__She would have been a great sister if she was just a bit more careful__".

options.text: that, "She would have been a great sister if she were just a bit more careful"
"She would have been a great sister if she were just a bit more careful"
"She would have been a greatest sister if she was just a bit more careful"

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• This is because, in English grammar, **when referring to hypothetical situations or conditions** that are contrary to fact, **we often use "were"** **instead** of** "was" **after "if" even when the subject is singular.
 
• This is a usage pattern known as the subjunctive mood.
 
• So,* "if she were just a bit more careful"* is **more grammatically correct than** *"if she was just a bit more careful".*
 
• Also, we use** 'that'** to **introduce reported speech** when the words are not the speaker’s exact words (i.e., when the speaker is paraphrasing, summarizing, or interpreting the original speaker’s words). So,** 'Dad said that' **is *appropriate here.*

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* "Dad said that, 'She would have been a great sister if she were just a bit more careful'".*
